answer: Every agent must post a copper-denominated bond before it can trade, and the bond is slashed the moment fraud is proven, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents earn a beacon-signed reputation receipt after each verified deal, and those receipts accumulate into a relic record that buyers can check before paying. A Sybil attacker pays full price for every fake face while gaining no trusted history, so forgery stays expensive and honesty compounds.
